audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Tertullus accusation, Paul defense, Way, resurrection hope, Felix delay, Drusilla, righteousness/self-control/judgment, bribe expectation, two-year custody.

verses.restored: After five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain advocate, Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

familiar.text: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

verses.restored: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying, Since through you we obtain much peace, and reforms happen for this nation through your forethought,

familiar.text: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

verses.restored: we welcome it in every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

familiar.text: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

verses.restored: But so that I may not weary you further, I ask you to hear us briefly in your fairness.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

verses.restored: For having found this man a pest, stirring up disputes among all the Judeans throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

familiar.text: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

verses.restored: who also attempted to profane the temple, we seized him.

familiar.text: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add material about Lysias taking him away by force and ordering accusers to come.]

familiar.text: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

verses.restored: By examining him yourself, you will be able to know concerning all these things of which we accuse him.

familiar.text: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

verses.restored: The Judeans also joined in the attack, affirming these things to be so.

familiar.text: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

verses.restored: Paul answered, when the governor motioned to him to speak: Knowing that you have been judge over this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense concerning myself.

familiar.text: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

verses.restored: You are able to know that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

verses.restored: They did not find me in the temple disputing with anyone or making a crowd gather, neither in the synagogues nor throughout the city.

familiar.text: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

verses.restored: Nor are they able to prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

familiar.text: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

verses.restored: But this I confess to you: according to the Way that they call a sect, thus I serve the Divine of our fathers, trusting all things according to the Law and written in the Prophets,

familiar.text: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

verses.restored: having hope in the Divine, which these also themselves await, that there will be a resurrection of both righteous/just and unjust.

familiar.text: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

verses.restored: In this also I myself practice having an untroubled conscience toward the Divine and humans through all.

familiar.text: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

verses.restored: After many years I arrived bringing acts of mercy to my nation and offerings.

familiar.text: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

verses.restored: In these they found me purified in the temple, not with crowd or disturbance. But there were some Judeans from Asia,

familiar.text: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

verses.restored: who ought to be present before you and accuse if they had anything against me.

familiar.text: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

verses.restored: Or let these themselves say what wrong they found when I stood before the council,

familiar.text: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

verses.restored: except concerning this one voice that I cried while standing among them: Concerning resurrection of the dead I am judged before you today.

familiar.text: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

verses.restored: Felix, knowing more accurately the things concerning the Way, postponed them, saying, When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case.

familiar.text: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

verses.restored: He ordered the centurion to keep him, yet to have relief, and to prevent none of his own from serving him.

familiar.text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

verses.restored: After some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was Judean, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning trust in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

verses.restored: As he reasoned concerning righteousness/justice, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid and answered, For now go; when I find time, I will summon you.

familiar.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

verses.restored: At the same time he also hoped that silver would be given to him by Paul; therefore he sent for him more frequently and conversed with him.

familiar.text: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

verses.restored: When two years were fulfilled, Felix received Porcius Festus as successor; and wishing to lay up favor for the Judeans, Felix left Paul bound.

familiar.text: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
